levels.1: The executive summary has some points or claims that are not clear.
levels.2: A clear executive summary is provided. The main problem and approach are described, but some aspects could be more detailed or better articulated.
levels.3: A compelling and comprehensive executive summary is provided. The summary describes the problem well.

levels.0: The report does not clearly explain why this problem (or dataset) should be analyzed or studied.
levels.1: The report explains the problem and why it is relevant, but the motivation or significance could be more clearly justified.
levels.2: The report explains clearly and convincingly why this problem (or dataset) should be analyzed or studied.

levels.1: A few sources/articles are included, but they do not provide a good overview of the previous/related work.
levels.2: Relevant sources/articles are included and provide a general overview of related work, though the discussion lacks depth or strong connections to the project.
levels.3: The report includes meaningful articles/sources that explain the context and related work.

levels.1: The data collection is explained but several aspects are unclear or missing.
levels.2: The data collection process is described and mostly understandable, though some details or steps are not fully specified.
levels.3: The data collection process is comprehensively explained. The reader can understand clearly how the team collected the data.

levels.1: The report describes how data preprocessing was conducted. However, some aspects are not clear, confusing, or missing.
levels.2: The report explains the main preprocessing steps (e.g., cleaning, transformation), but some steps lack clarity, justification, or reproducibility.
levels.3: The report describes comprehensively how data was transformed, merged, imputed, etc. The reader can imagine and follow all the preprocessing steps that the team performed.

levels.0: The documentation is limited or unclear. The data source or context is only partially described, and key details about how the data was obtained or processed are missing. This makes it difficult to understand or trust the dataset.
levels.1: The dataset is generally documented, including its source and basic context. However, some details about data collection, assumptions, or limitations are missing or unclear. The documentation is understandable but does not fully support reproducibility.
levels.2: The dataset is thoroughly documented, including its origin, context, and purpose. The data source is clearly described, along with how the data was collected or generated. Any assumptions, limitations, and preprocessing decisions are explicitly stated. The documentation provides sufficient context for full understanding and reproducibility.

levels.0: The report does not explain fully which variables are features or target/class/dependent variables.
levels.1: The report identifies features and target variables, but the distinction or rationale is not fully clear or precise.
levels.2: The report explains which columns are features (independent variables) and which ones are the target/class/dependent variables.

levels.1: Only two [prediction / clustering / regression] algorithms and one model per algorithm. Algorithms and models’ parameters are not fully described.
levels.2: At least two algorithms are implemented with one model each. The models are described, but parameter choices or justifications are limited or partially explained.
levels.3: At least three [prediction / clustering / regression] algorithms and one model per algorithm. Algorithms and models’ parameters are well described and justified.

levels.1: The baseline is unclear or cannot be implemented or calculated.
levels.2: A baseline is defined and can be used for comparison, though it may not be fully justified or optimally chosen.
levels.3: The baseline is reasonable, and it can be used to compare machine learning models’ results.

levels.0: No answer is provided or only one metric is presented.
levels.1: Only two metrics are presented for all the models.
levels.2: At least two metrics are presented and used to evaluate the models, though the selection or interpretation of metrics could be more comprehensive.
levels.3: At least three metrics are presented for each model. Prediction task: Pr, Re, F1, AOC-ROC. Clustering task: SSE, Silhouette, Purity, etc. Estimation task: R2, F-statistic, AIC, BIC, etc.

levels.0: The discussion is superficial and does not offer any insights into the results.
levels.1: The discussion acknowledges the results with some analysis, offering a basic interpretation of their implications. However, it lacks depth in exploring alternative explanations or future research directions.
levels.2: The discussion summarizes the main findings and provides some interpretation of the results. However, the analysis lacks depth, critical reflection, or strong connections to the research problem and prior work.
levels.3: The discussion provides a thorough and insightful analysis of the results, integrating them with previous/related work.

levels.0: The report provides only superficial recommendations or implications.
levels.1: The report provides some recommendations and implications, but it lacks depth in providing actionable directions for the future.
levels.2: The report includes recommendations or implications based on the results, but they are somewhat general, lack strong justification, or are not fully supported by the analysis.
levels.3: The report provides relevant recommendations, develops thoughtful implications, and suggests specific actionable directions for the future.

levels.0: The code and data are not available/accessible.
levels.1: A GitHub repository is shared. Parts of the datasets and scripts are incomplete or not accessible. It is not possible to run the script on another computer (i.e., missing data, missing scripts).
levels.2: A GitHub repository is shared. Data and/or code are provided, but documentation is incomplete or unclear, making it somewhat difficult to reproduce the analysis or results.
levels.3: A GitHub repository is shared. All the datasets and scripts are accessible and complete. It is possible to run the script from another computer.

levels.0: The member misses one of the presentation days.
levels.1: The team presents an update of their work. However, it is not clear what actions the team will conduct. No preliminary results or models are presented.
levels.2: The team presents a comprehensive update of their work. However, there are minor issues with clarity, formatting, or quality that affect overall presentation.
levels.3: The team presents a comprehensive update of their work. Some models and preliminary results are discussed.
